en: ...Captain.
Yeah, thank you. I'm okay. I've\ncalmed down.
Are you feeling alright?
The facilities here couldn't\ninterfere with my body, so I\nself-repaired.
That's a bit blunt, but I'm just\nglad to see you're back to\nnormal.
I'm not sure if I'm "normal"...
...Captain, have you heard?

The Phantoms were supposed
to have been driven from this
universe by my father and the
Edge Mavericks.
The Ober Commander-in-Chief,\nAsmodeus.

Good grief. I thought I'd had
quite enough of trying to
negotiate directly with the big
boss of one side during a war.

...Based on what I've heard,
may I take it that you intend to
side with the Raza Space
Force?

Nya, that's not exactly it. We're
just going to meet this
Asmodeus person. I never said
anything about defeating them.

They are not someone you can
just go and meet so casually.
No matter how you look at it, it
will result in combat.
Though, as a result, you will be\ncontributing to the victory of\nthe Raza forces.

We aren't intervening in the
war between Raza and Ober.
We're just investigating a crisis
that might threaten the entire
universe.

I admit that is sophistry. If we
encounter Asmodeus, combat
is unavoidable, and if you call
that intervention, you are
correct.

If Raza ends up winning as a
result, we will be looked upon
with suspicion by the Ober
side. Even so...

This is no longer just an
intervention in the Azurite
system. It is a battle to protect
the entire universe.
Whether they are survivors or\nsomething newly born, I don't\nknow.

Of course, we won't borrow any
more strength from Jeanne or
Isabel. That would only
increase the degree of our
intervention.
Therefore, from here on, we will\nuse our own ship...
Wait!
Euwin? What's wrong?
Captain, everyone... I have word\nfrom Lavarnia.
I will...
Huh?
I will show you that I can carry\nyou all aboard the Overman!
But... as a Hardier Warrior of\nMorphus, I cannot leave them\nunchecked.

Captain. This isn't just an
interstellar war. It is a crisis
that threatens every living
thing in the universe.
I cannot run away from this\nfight. Please...
Yes, we understand. We came\nto confirm your decision, Valka.
Eh?
As those born on Earth, and as\nmembers of the Galactic\nFederation...

We find ourselves unable to
simply stand by and watch the
war between Raza and Ober
unfold.
Did... something happen?
It might not be as simple as\nending the war like we did with\nDaftine.

But even if we were to find Eve
and bring her back right now,
we cannot simply leave the
Azurite system.
...What does everyone else\nthink?

Everyone has different goals,
but we agree we cannot just
overlook the conflict between
Raza and Ober.
I see... that's a relief. I thought\nRicardo might be against it.
We thought so too. But Ricardo\nwas actually the first one to\nagree.
What?

He suspected a link to
whoever shot down Ricardo
and Tika's spacecraft 200
years later.

The Azurite system 200 years
from now should be peaceful
per Ricardo's knowledge, so I
doubt there's a direct
connection, but...
No, that's fine. With this many\nallies, everyone is bound to\nhave different perspectives.

As long as the core
reason―that we can't ignore
the war between Raza and
Ober―remains, I think that's
enough.
You're absolutely right.
involving Heath, Lavarnia, and\nKevin as well.
Yeah, I'm fine. I can go now...

I must conduct myself in a way
that doesn't bring shame to
being a Hardier Warrior of
Morphus.
That's the spirit!
<font color=yellow>Missing Procedure</font>, is it?

Yeah. An "unknown will" that
transforms the laws of the
universe and changes the very
nature of existence itself.
Our Morphus guide, "Ex," called\nit the Missing Procedure.

That Phantom fleet analyzes
the energy information of
lifeforms that naturally exist
throughout this entire universe,
and replaces them with\nimmutable existences.

Turning lifeforms into
immutable beings? That's a
massive claim. Are you saying
Ober is messing with such an
incomprehensible existence?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> If it's like the Missing
Procedure my father faced,
then someone in Ober is likely
being manipulated.

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Since you can analyze it
that deeply, does that mean a
countermeasure for this
situation is already
established?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Of course. The Phantoms
have a source of origin. I
propose that we track down
and destroy that source.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> A source of origin... so\nyou mean there's something\nlike a nest for them.

<font color=blue>Valka</font> You are correct. To be
precise, the substance "Grigori"
absorbs surrounding
information to create
Phantoms.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Grigori?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> You can imagine it as a\ncrystal-like stone that glows\npurple.

They vary in size, but based on
Captain Jeanne's account, if
it's like the previous battle, it
should be quite large.
<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> So, you're saying if we\nsmash that Grigori, those\nPhantoms will just vanish?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> That is correct. However,\nI have one question.

Even so, I find it hard to
believe that Ex would have
overlooked a Grigori of such
massive proportions.
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Good grief, here he\ngoes again with his praise for\nEx.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Mastima!

<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...Given Morphus's
history, the threat of this
Grigori is on a completely
different level than Master
Mastima's Moonshadow Ladder.

If this were truly caused by the
Grigori, I'd have been sent to
the Azurite system. The threat
level is juuuust tooooooo
different!

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> What!? Those ghosts
are a bigger threat than my
Moonshadow Ladder!? Take it
back, you little pet of
Vandione!
<font color=blue>Verda</font> You're competing over\nthe wrong things...
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Mastima! Just be quiet!\nWe can't make any progress!

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Shut up, Tika! How am
I supposed to stay quiet after
being told something like
tha-ha-ha-ha...
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Honestly! Valka, please\ncontinue!
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Hehe. Anyway, there are\nmany unnatural aspects to this\nPhantom incident.

But if I recall correctly, even
before we entered this Azurite
system, we had already seen
things similar to the Phantoms.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> ...The black monsters Givel\nsummons. ...And... Eve's...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Mmmph! Mmmph!!
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Maaaastima! Be quiet!!
<font color=blue>Henri</font> So you're saying Givel is\nthe one currently creating\nthese Phantoms?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> I'd like to say that's the\ncase... but even so, questions\nremain.
Givel's goal in Daftine was to\ncross the boundary between\nadjacent universes.
That is why Thornite, which\nstabilizes space, should have\nbeen a vital element for him.
However, in Lazuli, the\nPhantoms and Thornite were in\nconflict.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Now that you mention it,\nthat's true.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Those guys showed\nsome real guts against that\nblack McKinley ship.

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Besides, Phantoms are
hostile to all life. It's
inexplicable why they are
currently acting only in Ober's
favor.
The problem lies in the footage\nof Lady Leash that Lady Carlin\nsummoned at the Urza System.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> You mean the one\nwhere Eve saw Givel?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> If that footage was
recorded after defeating Givel,
then the person appearing
alongside him likely holds the
key to this situation.

<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> Are you saying someone
is manipulating Givel, just like
he manipulated the Beast
Witches?
To think someone could\nactually do that to Givel...
It is possible.
Eh?

There is one person who might
be able to. If my and the
Captain's speculation is
correct.

I heard from Jeanne. That the
current Commander-in-Chief of
the Ober Space Force is
named Asmodeus.

If there is an existence capable
of doing something to Givel, it
can be none other than
Asmodeus!

Asmodeus is the Demon King
of planet Roak at the galaxy's
edge, a ruler who led monster
armies to exterminate humanity
there.
The demon realm, huh?\nMastima was spouting\nsomething like that before.
It is said that Asmodeus was a\nbeing that harbored hatred for\nall of humanity.

Leading the Ober
humans―called monsters
elsewhere―they've long been
enemies of the humans on
planet Roak.

...In the footage we saw from
the Urza System, there was
someone else near Givel,
wasn't there?
You're saying that silhouette is\nAsmodeus?
I believe that is a strong\npossibility.
Regardless of whether we are\ninvestigating the secrets of the\nPhantom,
Or searching for Eve and Givel,\nthe clue we must pursue is...
A few hours later―
Is the Overman repaired\nalready?
...Yeah. Isabel's engineers took\ncare of all the major repairs.
It's frustrating, but experts\nreally are something else.
I see, that's a relief.
...Euwin. Aren't you supposed to\nbe at the meeting?
I still don't understand all the\ncomplicated space talk.

I figured it's enough for me to
just know that we might end
up fighting the past grudges of
our comrades.
...You're taking this quite lightly,\naren't you?
Because I know the captains'\njudgment won't be wrong.

More importantly, I came
looking for Welch. I was worried
after she slipped away from
the meeting...

...She's fine. Welch is over
there, quietly listening to an
Isabel technician explain how
the Warp Drive works.

That's a relief. I was worried
she might be messing around
with something of Isabel's
without permission.

She seemed to enjoy watching
the Overman being repaired.
There was nothing for you to
worry about, Euwin.
If you say so... but, I'm truly\nsorry.
Eh?
Because of our circumstances,\nwe ended up breaking the\nOverman.
...It's okay. It's being fixed, so\nI'm not dwelling on it anymore.

Even so, you've been working
hard to build this ship bit by
bit for a long time, haven't you,
Lavarnia?
after selecting every single\npart for the Overman yourself.
...It's not your fault, Euwin. I'm\nthe one who decided to take\neveryone out into space.
...Thank you.
...You're the first person to\never say something like that to\nme.
Pardon?
In terms of specs, the Overman\nisn't actually that great of a\nship.
Is that so?
I think Coro's presence\nimproved its software\nperformance,

But even so, a ship built and
maintained properly in the
Bazaar docks is probably much
more superior.

Without a military-grade
transporter, the Overman
wouldn't have been forced into
these trades if it weren't for
Eve.
I see...
When Papa saw me tuning the\nOverman, he tried to give me\nlots of good parts.
But I turned him down.\nBecause if I did that...
...Euwin, you really respect the\nfeelings of those who create\nthings, don't you?
That's just how Welch has\nalways been.
...Welch did?

Welch's family are blacksmiths,
and she's been caught up in all
sorts of tool-making since she
was young.
So she wasn't helping, she was\nbeing "caught up" in it.
Caught up, yeah. She's been\nused as a test subject for all\nkinds of things.
Hehe, I see.
While making all those different\nthings, Welch always insisted\non making something "original."

Sometimes she'd even close
the shop for a long time,
saying she wanted to gather
the materials herself,

And she was so determined to
one day make a sword that
surpassed the blueprints Coro
gave me.
That eventually led to me,\nsomeone from an unmapped\nplanet, taking flight into space.
And thanks to that, Welch...\nshe found friends who truly\nunderstand her.
...Eh? D-do you mean me?

Once the Captain's troubles
are resolved and we return to
the Stardust Bazaar, I hope
you'll still be friends with
Welch.
...Wait, what do you mean?

We got Heath back to the
mothership, but now we're
heading straight into the war
between Raza and Ober.
...No way.

Of course, we'll properly
compensate you for the ships
Eve destroyed and the Gems
that were stolen.
...That's... forget it.
Huh?

I've received more than enough
for the stones. I even have
change left from the broken
ships. So...
If you'll have me, I want you to\ncome with me and board the\nOverman from here.
W-wait, Lavarnia! You don't\nmean you're going to... with us...
It's dangerous! To be honest, I\nhave no idea what's going to\nhappen next!
Wait, hold on, are you okay,\nEuwin?! Welch, a wrench just\nhit him in the head...!
It's fine, it's fine. Eu-boy isn't\ngonna die from something like\nthis.
Ugh...! I will die! If it had hit me\nin a bad spot, I would've died!!
You didn't die because it hit\nyou in a good spot, obviously.
More importantly, Eu-boy! I\ndon't remember raising you to\nbe such a heartless man!

I don't remember being raised
is how you say it! You're being
completely nonsensical as
usual!

You just confessed to Lover
that "I've been volunteering for
beautiful girl Welch-chan's
experiments since way back
when."
I never said a single word of\nthat!!
Yeah, yeah, whatever. Anyway,\nLover says they want to come\nwith us.
What?! No, I mean... there's no\nreason for Lavarnia to go\ndiving into danger like that...!
I want to challenge the world\nwith something I created.\nThat's reason enough!
Whaaaat!?

We're going to be smashing
those black-clad bastards or
searching for Eve and Givel
anyway, right?
But you're not going to go\naround explaining all that to\nthe people of Raza or Ober.
That's... probably true.

Daftine might set her sights on
you by the people of Raza and
Ober who don't know the
situation.
Th-that's...

If you don't want to take sides
between Raza and Ober, you
won't be able to ride Isabel
around however you like, either.
So, which ship can we move\nfreely right now, and who is its\nowner?
...Welch.
...That's, well, yeah... But, it's\nnot like I'm not knowing my\nplace...

If you understand, then move!
Before the captains even think
about summoning Rekoro, go
stop them!
O-Okay, okay! Just stop\nswinging that wrench around!
...Um, Welch, why?
Because it looked like they\nwere having fun. Obviously.
Eh?
Flying through space in your\nown ship... it must have been\nfun.

After all, you built it yourself,
so I get it. It's a great feeling
seeing something you made
actually doing its job!
...Welch.

Can you stick with me a little
longer? My captains, Coro,
Euwin, Verda, Tika, Karlyn,
Valka, Henri, and Ricardo...

They always want to shoulder
everything. Even when not
asked, they act all serious and
try to take on unnecessary
trouble.

Being thoughtless is bad, but
it's time they realized that
using what's already available
isn't a bad thing.
I wish they'd learn a thing or\ntwo from Mastima in that\nregard.
...Hey, Welch.
Hmm?

For now, we have no choice
but to use this Overman, even
though it's been modified for
Raza,
But once everything is over... I\nwant to build a new ship from\nscratch. Will you help me?
Of course! I'd be delighted!

Come on, Lover, go on. If you
don't give them the okay, our
stiff-necked crew will stay
suspicious.
...Okay!
Are you being serious?
Yes, Boss!
...Are you serious?
...Y-Yes, Boss!!
I sense hesitation.
Yes, Boss!!! I'm going with them!
Is that not a violation of\nservice regulations?
You fired me, Boss! I'm not\neven a soldier anymore!!
I see. I will not allow it.
Why?! That was supposed to\nbe the part where you let it\nslide!!

They are not villains. I
understand they possess
superior technology and that
each one is a powerful warrior.
But this is war, and there are\nno guarantees. I won't send my\nsubordinates to their deaths.
Boss! But...!
Furthermore, it is a promise I\nmade to your parents.
...Therefore, I will absolutely not\npermit you to accompany them.
Boss... I...
Eek!? W-what was that?
Listen to me, Heath Bureau. I\nwill not permit it.
Huh?
I must uphold my promise to\nyour parents. I will not allow\nyou to go with them.

Since Isabel is no longer
charged with treason, I won't
assign my subordinates to
excessively dangerous missions
anymore.
...Boss...
Unlike back then, you are an\nadult now. I will not permit this.
...Yes, Boss!!
If you understand, then return\nto your previous post as\nordered.
Yes, Boss!! Thank you so\nmuch!!

I have done nothing to be
thanked for. You know exactly
what happens to those who
disobey my orders... don't you?
Yes, Boss! Excuse me!!

...Good grief. To make the
"Demon of Marswest" say all
that... they are incredibly
dense. I hope they don't
become a hindrance.
The vigor of the youth is quite\ndazzling to an old man like me.
I am still quite young myself.
Of course, I include you in that.\nIn my eyes, all Raza people are\nlike children.
If you truly are the one and\nonly Kevin Barktain, then I\nsuppose that may be true.
In all honesty, do you really\nbelieve they can achieve their\ngoal?

It is an old man's duty to
believe in the young. We have
spent our lives acting superior
to them, so we shouldn't make
things difficult for them.
...I see.

Yes. We must do what we must
do. We have to at least clear a
path for the children to walk
upon.
...But, are you certain? Your\nship's position will only worsen\nfrom here.

It's too late. Our position hasn't
improved. Being tasked to fill
the gaps in this desperate war
is practically the same as
being sentenced for treason.

...Then, on our way, I shall
present the research I've
accumulated in Lazuli. I am
sure you will find it quite
enjoyable.
All crew members, confirm\nharness attachment. Overman,\ndeparting!

Systems all green. No
spacecraft or excess
silicon-based matter detected
nearby. The area should be
safe for now.

Alright, let's plan our next
move. Thanks to Isabel and her
crew, we know the battle
situation, but we're heading out
blind to our own status.
We don't even know where Eve\nis; how can we track down\nGivel or Asmodeus?
I have an idea regarding that.\nPlease, let me!
Hmm?

I have been waiting for this
communication. I have just
finished constructing the
requested program.
Rekoro!
I have already completed the\ncreation of a full star chart for\nthe Azurite system.

With this, we can narrow down
the location of the "Grigori" or
the Phantom fleet's command
center to some extent.
What do you mean by that?

We will exploit the fact that
combat between Raza and
Ober is occurring incessantly
within the Azurite system.

The method is simple. We just
observe the Raza's combat
status across the star system
and the concentration of
silicon-based matter, but...

I see. If the Raza ships are
engaging despite no reaction
from the Ober ships, the
Phantom is likely there.

Exactly. We are also receiving
feedback from Coro regarding
the current specs of the
Overman.

Based on the Phantom's
location and ship specs, we'll
guide them toward the most
likely position of the command
tower.
Whoa, your ships still have\nabsolutely insane specs, as\nusual.
Of course they do. They were\nmodified using the full strength\nof the Ex Giva... Hm?
Yo. What's with the weird look\non your face?
Heath!? Why are you here!?

Huh!? Heath-san, you weren't
included in the weight
calculations when we left
Isabel!
...I left the Gems container\nbehind to pay for the\nOverman's repairs.
What!?
What were you thinking, after\nwe finally managed to return to\nthe mothership?

What am I thinking? It's
obvious. I'm thinking about
protecting the peace of the
universe I was born in.
Heath...

During the meeting, you all
obsessed over distant cosmic
karma, but this is the Azurite
system where I was born.

You're all fighting a cosmic
crisis from the Azurite system.
As someone born here, I can't
just sit back and do nothing.
Did you get permission from\nthe boss?
There's no way my boss would\ngive me permission.
Hmph, I see.
No way! That would mean it's a\nviolation of orders...

The moment I was cast out in
that lifeboat, I stopped being a
soldier. Orders don't even
apply to me anymore.
Whether some superior officer\nforgives a non-soldier or not\nhas nothing to do with me.

Eu-chan, you used that same
logic to stand up to your folks,
didn't you? You've gotten all
stiff lately, probably because
life's been so peaceful.
Ugh... No, well, I mean...
There's no reason why I can't\nact alongside Lover just like\nyou guys are.

And then there's Lover's old
man. If she gets hurt, he won't
stop until he's destroyed both
Raza and Ober.
Protecting Lover is directly\nlinked to protecting the peace\nof the Azurite system.

...I'm not so weak that I need
Heath to protect me, and he's
being quite selfish, but I figured
if I refused, he'd only act more
recklessly, so I had no choice.

...Since Ms. Lavarnia owns this
ship, I'll comply, but weight
calculations are scary. Please
let me know next time...
...Understood.

Anyway, if we use Rekoro's
analysis to crush the Phantoms
one by one, we'll eventually run
into their nest.
And if your enemies, Givel or\nCommander Asmodeus, are\ninvolved with the Phantoms,

They might eventually lose
their patience and show their
tails. We just need to catch
them then!
That is how it is.
Simple and easy to understand.\n...Hey, Captain.

I said that earlier, but I'm Raza.
I have many buddies in Ober,
and that old man from
Stardust Bazaar is the one
who saved my life.

I'm not thinking of anything as
grand as stopping the war, but
if something is eroding the
Azurite system behind it, I want
to stand against it.
So, let me join you.
Yeah. Heath, it's good to have\nyou on board!
Crew registration... well, since\nwe're on the Overman right\nnow, we should be fine.
Is the discussion concluded?\nVery well, I shall transmit the\nprimary analysis.

Fortunately, a Phantom is
expected near the Overman.
Please rush to one of the
points immediately.
Hell yeah! Let's go!

Don't just take charge! I'm the
captain now. Change course
toward the Phantom ship's
predicted location, full speed
ahead!
Roger!!

After analyzing the AI Rekoro
data, we've narrowed it down.
There are eight points with a
high frequency of appearance.

That's fewer than I expected. I
thought they'd be appearing in
massive swarms all over the
place.

Maybe the Raza military ships'
sensors struggle to detect
silicon, even though it's a
common substance in space.
On top of that, their black\nexterior makes visual\nconfirmation difficult as well.

But the Raza aren't just sitting
idly by. It seems their fleet
hasn't taken much damage
from the battles these past
few days.

Exactly. So, after consulting
with the Captain, Administrator
Koro, Mista Heath, and Lady
Lavarnia,

We have narrowed these eight
points down to three locations
where the command center
might be.

Near Lazuli," "Space Base
Clusters," and the "Asteroid
Belt"? Why these three
locations?

Fighting near Lazuli is always
flashy. With so many Ober
ships out there, a Phantom
pilot could easily hide among
them.
...As for the second one, this is\nan area with many Ober\nmilitary space bases.

However, compared to other
areas, they're repelling Raza
ships at a high rate relative to
their defensive strength.
As for the last one, it is a small\nmining asteroid belt.

It should be an abandoned
place with very little ore, yet
every once in a while, Raza
ships report damage here.
If we've narrowed down the\nlocations, are we starting the\noperation immediately?

Yes. I don't know if Asmodeus
or Givel are here, or if the
Grigori Valka mentioned exists,
but...

The longer we wait, the more
Raza casualties we'll see. We
must strike every point as
soon as it's identified.
Alright, I'm itching for a fight!
...This might not be a situation\nwhere you can do anything\nthrough hand-to-hand combat.
Still itching!

...Sigh. The enemy isn't just the
Phantom. And that doesn't
mean the Raza or Ober ships
are our allies, either.
...I forgot about that!
...Honestly.
Is that guy really going to be\nokay?
Well, his skills are certainly\nreliable... So, Captain. Where\nshall we strike first?
Uwaaaaaaaah! Aaaaaah!
Optical weapons approaching\nfrom Course 121 Mark 54!
A swarm of Wormhole Insects\nhas been launched from the\nOber combat fleet behind us!
Detected a cluster of naval\nmines ahead, likely Raza! Take\nevasive action!
Found 'em! Course 28 Mark 80,\ndistance 240!

I had visual on the Phantom
squad, and then―bam! They're
gone! Hey, Lover, put it back!
Put it back!
Ughhhhhhh!? Aaaaaah!?
Ugh... my head is... spinning...\n*gag*...

Th-this is way beyond just
dealing with Phantoms!
Enemies are coming from every
direction! Whaaa?!
Hey! We're being swarmed by\nthose Ober bugs! Someone go\nexterminate them!

It's impossible with all this
shaking! I feel like I'll be blown
right out of my seat if I try to
stand up! Waaaaah?!
You'll bite your tongue if you\nkeep talking! Welch! Euwin! Put\nthese on!

The gravity and inertia are
being adjusted to match the
Overman's maneuvers! You
should be able to walk!
R-really!?

Hurry up! The bulkhead near
the Warp Drive is breached! If
they get into the drive itself,
there's no telling what will
happen!
I-I get it, I get it! I'm going,\nokay!?
Heh. How pitiful, those who are\nbound by inertia and gravity.
Why are you acting so cool\nabout this!? If you're so fine,\nthen come with us!
Good grief.
...In a situation like this, the\nones floating should be the\nones in danger...
